title: Finance policy overhaul and community safety plan
subtitle: Asset management policy, enterprise risk register, City Clerk's Office profile, staff recognitions and election preparations
overview: The Committee of the Whole recommended a consolidated set of finance policies. Three older policies on budget monitoring, revenue budgeting and year-end surplus allocation would be repealed, with their content folded into a restructured budget policy and a new user fees and charges policy {{vote:m4}}. The committee also recommended adopting the 2026–2029 Community Safety and Well-being Plan, which sets six priority risk areas {{vote:m5}}.

The committee recommended approving an update to the Corporate Asset Management Policy to meet provincial regulation O.Reg 588/17. It also received the 2026 Enterprise Risk Management register update for information {{vote:m3}}. Economic uncertainty and aging infrastructure remain the highest-rated risks.

For residents, the finance changes could allow routine inflation-based adjustments to user fees without annual Council reports. The safety plan relies on existing agency work because no provincial funding comes with it. The committee also heard a City Clerk's Office profile, including staffing pressure on freedom of information work and the opening of recruitment for election-day workers. After a closed session on a natural gas franchise agreement and a Downtown planning matter before the Ontario Land Tribunal, the minutes report only that Council gave direction to staff. Council will consider all recommendations at a later meeting.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended approving updated budget, user fees and charges, debt management, and reserve and reserve fund policies, and repealing the budget monitoring, revenue budgeting and year-end surplus allocation policies.
The committee recommended adopting the 2026–2029 plan, which sets six priority risk areas including homelessness and affordable housing, and mental health and substance use.
The committee recommended approving an update to the policy to meet the requirements of O.Reg 588/17.
The committee received the 2026 Enterprise Risk Management risk register update for information.

debate: On the risk register, one councillor raised aging infrastructure. Staff said renewal funding has risen but more slowly than costs, so the funding gap and backlog have grown. They said options would come back in the next strategic plan and multi-year budget cycle.

Staff said the City's tax-supported contingency reserves are well below target and that year-end surpluses meant to rebuild them have not materialized. Development charge collections were also below forecast early in the year.

On the finance policies, a councillor asked why the reserve policy names only the police service and public library. Staff said only those two boards hold reserves managed under the policy. Social housing pressures are handled through other City reserves.

On the safety plan, councillors asked how change can happen with no dedicated funding. Staff said the plan focuses on actions agencies already carry out, with the advisory table meeting twice a year and progress reviewed annually. Councillors also asked how to measure progress on gender-based violence, since more reporting can look like more incidents, and asked for housing targets in the next update.

In the Clerk's Office profile, the City Clerk said the freedom of information, privacy and records team is two people. Without added resources, the office expects to miss new statutory timelines in 2027. Councillors also asked about election integrity and voter identification.
